title: Breakpoints and async stacks in one minute
purpose: Recall which breakpoint answers which question, and how the async call stack explains a race.
sequence_reason: The summary follows the order of a real debugging session, from the symptom to the evidence.
summary: The summary replays the session. The symptom was a stale list. A fetch breakpoint showed two requests in flight. A conditional breakpoint paused only on the stale response. Stepping showed render writing the old label, and async frames showed which input event started the stale request.
explanation: Choose the breakpoint by the question you ask. The Call Stack with async frames tells you which earlier call caused the code that is paused now.

learning_check.question: You see a wrong request URL. Which breakpoint finds the code that sends it?
learning_check.answer: An XHR/fetch breakpoint with part of the URL as its string.

scenes.heading: What you found
scenes.narration: The stale list came from a slow response that arrived last.

scenes.heading: Pick the breakpoint by the question
scenes.narration: Use a line-of-code breakpoint when you know the line. Add a condition to skip pauses you do not need. Use a fetch breakpoint when you know only the URL.

items: Conditional: pause only when it matters
XHR/fetch: you know part of the URL
DOM change: you know the element

scenes.heading: Read the pause
scenes.narration: At each pause, Scope shows the local values, Watch tracks your own expression, and the Call Stack shows how the code got there.

visual.verdict: Values say what is wrong; the stack says where it came from.

scenes.heading: From evidence to fix
scenes.narration: The evidence points to the fix. The code must ignore a response whose query no longer matches the box.
